idiom_name: shared symbol brand tested with `sym in obj`
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no interfaces or run-time types, so the substitute for a marker is a brand: a shared symbol (Symbol.for, so the identity survives separate module instances and realms) set on the prototype and tested with `sym in obj`; well-known symbols such as Symbol.iterator play exactly this role for language protocols, and Symbol.toStringTag brands built-ins for Object.prototype.toString. Use a symbol brand to gate brand-sensitive operations; the key is hidden from Object.keys and JSON.stringify, and the prototype chain makes subclass instances inherit the mark.
pitfalls: Symbol() creates a new symbol per call and per realm; Symbol.for registers globally, so a key collision silently shares the mark.
A plain object literal can forge the brand - symbols hide the key but do not make it unforgeable.
JSON.stringify and Object.keys skip symbol-keyed marks, which is usually desired but surprising when serializing.

variants.name: WeakSet brand registry
variants.implementation_notes: A module-private WeakSet records the objects created through the marking API, so consumers ask the registry instead of inspecting the object: the brand cannot be forged, does not appear on the instance, and does not keep objects alive. This is the standard hardening for capability gates such as 'only validated values may reach the DOM sink'. Membership does not transfer to clones, proxies or structured clones, so validate values that re-enter.
pitfalls: WeakSet membership is per-realm and per-registry: copies, proxies and structured clones are not branded.
Only objects (and, since ES2023, non-registered symbols) can be WeakSet members - primitives cannot be branded.
A WeakSet does not keep objects alive, so 'branded' is not a retention guarantee; the brand disappears with the object.
